newsitem.title: USA: Clinton sex case trial may start within year-lawyers.
newsitem.headline: Clinton sex case trial may start within year-lawyers.

text.p: Lawyers for Paula Jones said on Tuesday that a trial in her sexual harassment lawsuit against President Bill Clinton could start within a year but they remained open to a settlement to restore her reputation.
The trial could begin "within a year," certainly before Clinton leaves office in three years, attorney Gilbert Davis, told a news conference.

"We are anxious to move this case forward, as is Paula Jones," added Joseph Cammarata, a second lawyer for the Long Beach, California, housewife and former Arkansas state employee who sued Clinton three years ago.
They spoke hours after the Supreme Court rejected a bid by Clinton to delay any proceedings in the case until after he leaves the White House.
Davis said any out-of-court settlement "is up to our opponents, if they choose, to proffer ... and we would certainly take it to our client to consider."

He said Jones's "primary interest ... is the redemption of her reputation. That is a central element of any settlement." He said any offer of a settlement should include an apology and a statement that Jones did nothing wrong.

Davis said previous negotiations with the White House before she sued Clinton "came close to a settlement." But he said the White House pulled the rug out from under the proposed settlement by issuing a "false statement to the press" in the matter.
"Our client wanted to settle this without filing a lawsuit," Davis said. He also said she was not out for money and pledged to donate any monetary settlement to charity. The lawsuit sought $700,000.

Cammarata said he was prepared to start gathering evidence, including issuing subpoenas and taking testimony from witnesses, perhaps including Clinton himself. He said his investigation could move beyond the incident Jones alleged to encompass other activities by the former Arkansas governor that might show a "pattern of conduct."

Asked if that might result in a trial with a stream of lurid allegations raining down on a sitting president, Cammarata said the federal court in Little Rock where the case would be tried "is not a forum where there's going to be a spectacle."
He said records from the Arkasas governor's office, the Arkansas state police and the Excelsior Hotel in Little Rock might be among the information he would seek.

Jones's lawsuit accused Clinton of making unwanted advances toward her at the Excelsior Hotel in 1991 when he was governor of Arkansas and she was a state employee. Clinton denied the allegations. The Supreme Court made no ruling on the merits of her case, but said it should be allowed to proceed.
"What the Supreme Court has reaffirmed is that every public official remains accountable for their personal and private conduct," Cammarata said.
He added that Jones has "gone through hell" and when she was informed of the court decision "she was excited, she was very elated ... she's anxious to have her day in court."
